headline: A weak US 30Y auction, oil at a new high and Fed hike talk push the US 10Y up 12bp to 5.10%; KTBs follow at about half the beta, the 10Y rising 6.4bp back above 4% to 4.001% as foreigners sell 10Y futures and 3s10s steepens off its low
summary: KTBs sold off with a long-end lead: the 3Y rose 3.0bp to 3.759%, the 10Y 6.4bp to 4.001% (51st percentile of its 1-year range) and the 20Y and 30Y 5.9bp each to 4.104% and 4.074%, while the 50Y added only 2.3bp to 4.049% after a fully covered auction. 3s10s steepened 3.4bp to 24.2bp from Thursday's 1-year low, and on the week the 3Y and 10Y are both about +15bp, the 10Y now −0.7bp month to date. Bills edged up: MSB 91-day 3.202% and CP 3.84% at 1-year highs, CD flat at 3.37%, so CP–CD is 47bp (92nd percentile). Spread products tightened as KTBs cheapened: the KDB 3Y fit fell 8bp to 13bp over (20th), AAA bank 1Y is 39.6bp (84th), AA- 3Y 67.5bp (69th) and KEPCO 3Y 40.6bp (78th).
drivers: US Treasuries: a 12bp overnight sell-off explains nearly all of it

The US 10Y rose 12bp to 5.10% on Nov 12, its first close above 5% since late October, after a soft 30Y auction (5.441%, a small tail, bid-to-cover 2.36 vs 2.54) and Fed speakers calling for more tightening. At the 1-year beta of 0.47 that implies +5.6bp for the KTB 10Y against an actual +6.4bp, so about 88% was global and under 1bp local. The KTB–UST 10Y gap widened to −110bp, a fresh 1-year extreme (0th percentile).
Foreigners sell 10Y futures again; futures trade cheap to fair

Foreigners sold 3,254 10Y futures and a token 40 3Y. The 10Y future fell 60 ticks to 108.10, 8 ticks below our basket fair value of 108.18 (2 ticks on Thursday), the 3Y 8 ticks to 103.42 (14 under fair 103.56) and the 30Y 154 ticks to 115.24, 39 ticks cheap. Cheap futures show selling led by hedges rather than cash, and late cash buying capped the move.
Oil and Iran add an inflation leg

WTI rose about 3% to near USD 89 after the US president said a deal with Iran was not needed and Houthi attacks hit Saudi oil sites; US December hike odds stayed fully priced with a small chance of 50bp. Japan's 10Y also rose 7bp, so the move was global, not Korean.
KOSPI −1.0% and a 50Y auction that held up

KOSPI reversed from 5,504 intraday to close −0.98% at 5,290.53 as foreigners sold about KRW 0.55–0.70tn, mostly SK Hynix (−3.0%), on AI-financing worries after the Nvidia CEO change. The KRW 700bn 50Y auction, the first since the dealer fines, was fully absorbed at a 160% bid-to-cover (246% in October), and the 50Y outperformed: 30s50s re-inverted to −2.5bp.
data: Softer demand but no tail; 50Y beat 30Y.
Solid headline; no change to BOK pricing.
Unanimous hold at 3.00%; a majority open to more tightening
Foreign KRW bond flows, October (KOFIA, Nov 10)
Big long now being trimmed via futures.
view: This week was a Treasury week: the US 10Y rose about 26bp from last Friday and at the weekly beta of 0.59 that accounts for roughly all of the KTB 10Y's +14.8bp, while over four weeks the US 10Y is unchanged and the KTB's −18.1bp is entirely Korea's own rally.

Locally the picture still favours bonds: the weekly rotation signal is +1.38 (daily +1.46), margin credit is −20% over four weeks and KOSPI fell back below 5,300, but foreigners are cutting their October KTB long through futures, which trade 8–14 ticks cheap.
I expect the 10Y in a 3.90–4.10% range into the BOK meeting; the add at 4.00% was filled today, so the long averages about 3.975%, 2.6bp against, stop 4.10%, target 3.85%.
I stay flat 3s10s: it steepened 3.4bp to 24.2bp on a global bear move, not a local re-steepening, and KOSPI did not hold 5,300.

Hedged is the better way to hold it: against 0.5 × US 10Y the long is about +0.9bp since Wednesday while outright is −5bp, and the signal's hedged record (rally calls right 67%, sell-off calls 69%, Sharpe 1.31, worst drawdown −26bp) beats outright (50%, 57%, 0.90, −36bp); a hot US PPI tonight is the main risk at about 0.5bp per Treasury bp.

buckets.name: KTB 1–2Y front end
buckets.why: The 2Y rose 2.0bp to 3.749%, 85th percentile of its 1-year range (average 3.39%), +14.8bp on the week; the 1Y +1.2bp to 3.631% (90th). 2s3s is 1.0bp (1st percentile, average 13bp) and 1s2s 11.8bp (7th). MSB 91-day (3.202%) and CP (3.84%) are at 1-year highs and price a November 26 hike to 3.25%.
buckets.call: Keep: buy the 2Y above 3.80%, target 3.65%, stop 3.90%. Not triggered (5bp away).

buckets.name: 3s10s curve
buckets.why: 3s10s steepened 3.4bp to 24.2bp from Thursday's 1-year low of 20.8bp (2nd percentile, average 40bp) as the long end followed Treasuries. The 3s5s10s fly fell to −7.8bp, a 1-year low (average 4.4bp), so the 5Y is the richest point on the curve. Our earlier steepener was stopped on Nov 5.
buckets.call: Stay flat: KOSPI closed at 5,290, below the 5,300 trigger. Re-enter the steepener (3 × 3Y vs 1 × 10Y futures, DV01 about KRW 86k each side) only if KOSPI regains 5,300 into Nov 17; target 32bp, stop 19bp.

buckets.name: KTB 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 4.001% is at the 51st percentile of a 3.25–4.60% range (average 3.92%). The add at 4.00% filled today, so the long from 3.95% plus 4.00% averages about 3.975%, 2.6bp against. Today's +6.4bp was about 88% Treasuries at the 0.47 beta; against 0.5 × US 10Y the hedged position is slightly positive since Wednesday.
buckets.call: Long, average 3.975%, stop 4.10%, target 3.85% (lowered from 3.80% with Treasuries above 5%); hold against about 0.5 × US 10Y. Open, −2.6bp outright.

buckets.name: Ultra-long 30–50Y
buckets.why: 30s50s re-inverted 3.6bp to −2.5bp (87th percentile, average −9.1bp) as the 50Y auction cleared and the 50Y rose only 2.3bp against 5.9bp for the 30Y, so the switch from +2.5bp is 5bp in favour, 0.5bp from target. The 10s20s30s fly is 13.3bp (76th), so the 20Y stays cheap; 20-2 2050 trades 9bp rich to the curve.
buckets.call: Keep the 30Y into 50Y switch from +2.5bp; target −3bp, stop moved to +0.5bp to lock in most of the gain. Open, +5bp.

buckets.name: KDB 1–3Y vs KTB
buckets.why: The KDB fit (32 trades) puts the 3Y 13.2bp over KTB, down 8bp on the day and at the 20th percentile (average 19.5bp), so the overweight from about 26bp hit its 20bp target. Part of the drop is the refit as KDB paper lagged the KTB sell-off; the 1Y fit is 29bp over (65th) and KOFIA's 1Y KDB quote 26.7bp (62nd). KEXIM has only 5 trades (low confidence).
buckets.call: Close: target 20bp hit (+12.8bp on the fit). Re-enter overweight only if the 3Y spread returns above 22bp.

buckets.name: AAA bank debentures and money market
buckets.why: AAA bank paper (55-trade fit) is 39.6bp over the 1Y KTB, 84th percentile (average 31bp), 0.4bp tighter; the 3Y is 31bp over (62nd). CP rose 1bp to 3.84% and CD held at 3.37%, so CP–CD is 47bp (92nd, average 28bp) and CD–MSB91 16.8bp (27th). IBK 1Y (49 trades) is 30.8bp over, 70th percentile.
buckets.call: No change: revisit bank paper once CP–CD falls below 35bp; prefer the 1Y over the 3Y if adding.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AA- 3Y)
buckets.why: AA- 3Y rose 2.7bp to 4.434%, slightly less than the KTB 3Y, so the spread is 67.5bp (69th percentile, average 61bp). KEPCO 3Y is 40.6bp over (78th, average 35bp) and BBB- minus AA- 582bp (68th). Credit lagged the KTB sell-off, as usual on rate-led days.
buckets.call: Add AA- only above 75bp or once KOSPI regains 5,300; no trigger hit.

watch: Next: US PPI (Nov 13, New York), the KRW 2.2tn KTB 10Y auction (Nov 16), Nvidia earnings and FOMC minutes next week, the college entrance exam on Nov 19 (KRX opens an hour late), Nov 1–20 exports around Nov 23, the BOK decision on Nov 26 (hike to 3.25% priced) and the FOMC on Dec 8–9; a hot PPI would hit KTBs at about 0.4–0.55bp per Treasury bp.
